newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares decline as investors take profits.
newsitem.headline: German shares decline as investors take profits.

text.p: German blue-chip shares slid on Thursday, as overnight losses on Wall Street sparked a mild bout of profit-taking and Bunds declined after the Bundesbank left interest rates unchanged.

The 30-share DAX index closed down 22.24 points at 2,680.75, while the IBIS DAX, which records day-long computer dealings, ended down 1.71 points at 2,683.52, well off the psychologically crucial 2,700 level defended earlier this week.
Dealers were divided on the market's next move, but agreed that there was no danger of a major rout.
"This is no giant weakness we're seeing here, just some uncertainty," said one Munich dealer.
Market interest focused on telecommunications and chemical sector shares.
Utilities firms Veba and RWE continued to rally after RWE said it would join Veba's alliance with British-based Cable & Wireless to create a challenger to monopoly Deutsche Telekom.
Veba ended late dealings up 1.06 marks pfennigs at 82.36 marks, while RWE was up 1.04 marks at 61.16 marks.

Utility firm Viag continued to slide after RWE said it would pull out of talks on a partnership with the Bavarian company and British Telecom and was not bucked even after it said the deal with BT would go ahead.
Viag ended floor dealings down 6.80 marks at 574.20 and closed the late electronic session at 575.50.
The chemicals and car sectors did worse than average and traders said both were affected by profit-taking.
One exception was sports carmaker Porsche which hit a bourse year high of 1,090 marks and ended the day up 24 marks at 1,089, following a positive profits report.

Carmaker Volkswagen, on the other hand, lost nine marks to end floor trade at 572.25 marks, paring its loss to 573.70 in later trade, after it said it was recalling 21,600 cars made at a plant in Portugal.
